title: Scotus dissents: venial penalty in hell eventually ends
source_text: XX. Scotus quidem aliter sensit. Nam in quartum Sententiarum, distinctione vigesima prima, docet peccato veniali, quod conjunctum permanet cum mortali, non deberi poenam aeternam in alia vita, sed tandem poenam illius in inferno finiri, permanente sola poena quae peccatis mortalibus debetur. Quaest. 1. parag. In ista quaestione.
pass_a_gloss: Scotus indeed thought otherwise. For in the fourth book of the Sentences, distinction twenty-one, he teaches that eternal punishment in the other life is not due to venial sin which remains joined with mortal, but that at length the punishment of that sin in hell is finished, while there remains only the punishment which is due to mortal sins. Question 1, paragraph In ista quaestione.
pass_b_english: Scotus alone here: venial penalty joined to mortal in hell finally ceases; only mortal debts remain forever.
Le Blanc flags him as the noted dissent before stating the common opposite.

choices.why: Named dissent from common School on hell’s venial penalty.
